aboutPage.title: About Thesion
aboutPage.aboutProjectText: Thesion is a hobby project created by Johan Resare to explore how a production app can be built with Claude Code (AI-assisted development). The app analyses stocks using established financial models and gives you personal investment suggestions.
aboutPage.technologyText: The entire app is built with AI-assisted development via Claude Code (Anthropic). The tech stack includes React for the frontend, Vercel for hosting, Supabase for database and authentication, Yahoo Finance for market data and Claude AI for the chat assistant.
aboutPage.contactText: Do you have questions, feedback or suggestions? Get in touch!
aboutPage.disclaimerText: Thesion does not provide financial advice. All information is for educational purposes. Always do your own research before investing.

intro.title: How does the scoring work?
intro.body:
Thesion uses a composite model based on five established financial methods.
Each stock is scored on a scale of 0-100. Your investor profile determines how the five sub-models are weighted.

piotroski.title: 1. Piotroski F-Score (Financial health)
piotroski.body: Developed by Professor Joseph Piotroski at Stanford. Tests 9 binary criteria to assess a company's financial strength:
items: Market cap above SEK 5 billion (not micro-cap)
piotroski.note: Score 0-9. Companies scoring 7-9 are considered financially strong. Weighted heavily for value investors.

magicFormula.title: 2. Magic Formula (Value)
magicFormula.body: Developed by Joel Greenblatt. Combines two key metrics to find undervalued quality companies:
items: Earnings Yield — earnings return (inverted P/E ratio). Higher = cheaper stock.
ROIC — return on invested capital. Higher = better capital allocation.
magicFormula.note: Sums earnings yield and ROIC into a combined score. Weighted heavily for value investors.

growth.title: 3. Growth score
growth.body: Assesses the company's growth potential through three components:
items: PEG ratio — P/E divided by growth rate. Below 1.0 indicates reasonably valued growth.
Revenue growth — percentage revenue growth. Above 15% is considered strong.
Operating margin — a high margin indicates scalability and operational leverage.

dividend.title: 4. Dividend score
dividend.body: Assesses the quality and sustainability of the company's dividend:
items: Dividend yield — current dividend relative to the share price. Above 3% gives a high score.
Sustainability — low debt + a good operating margin indicate that the dividend can be maintained.
Stability — low beta (volatility) suggests a stable dividend payer.

quality.title: 5. Quality score
quality.body: Universal quality indicator that works regardless of investment style:
items: Margin quality — combines operating and gross margin. High margins = competitive advantages.
ROIC quality — return on invested capital shows how efficiently the company uses its capital.
Debt — low debt/EBITDA indicates financial strength and flexibility.
quality.note: Weighted evenly for all profiles but extra heavily for growth and dividend investors.

weighting.title: Your profile determines the weighting
weighting.body: Depending on your investor profile, the five models are weighted differently:

riskAdjustment.title: Risk adjustment
riskAdjustment.body: The final score is adjusted based on how the stock's risk matches your risk profile:
items: Risk is assessed via Beta (volatility relative to the market). Beta < 0.8 = low risk, 0.8-1.2 = medium, > 1.2 = high.
If the stock's risk matches your profile: no adjustment.
1 step of deviation (e.g. you want low risk but the stock is medium): -8 points.
2 steps of deviation (e.g. you want low risk but the stock is high): -20 points.

dataSources.title: Data sources & updates
dataSources.body: All financial data is fetched from Yahoo Finance and Financial Modeling Prep (FMP). Scores are calculated daily at 07:00 CET on weekdays. The stock universe includes Nasdaq Stockholm Large Cap, Mid Cap and the 50 largest companies in the S&P 500.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: Thesion's scoring is an analysis tool, not financial advice. The models are based on historical and current financial data and cannot predict future price development. Always do your own research before investing. Thesion takes no responsibility for investment decisions based on this information.

interests.title: What interests you?

value.label: Value investor
value.explanation: You look for companies trading below their true value. Thesion prioritises companies with strong fundamentals — low P/E, high return on capital and solid cash flows.

growth.label: Growth investor
growth.explanation: You back companies with strong growth. Thesion prioritises fast-growing companies with high revenue growth and a scalable business model — even if they have a high P/E.

dividend.label: Dividend investor
dividend.explanation: You want recurring dividends. Thesion prioritises companies with a high and stable dividend yield, a long dividend history and a sustainable payout ratio.

index.label: Index investor
index.explanation: You prefer broad exposure. Thesion shows how your portfolio performs against the index and helps you find complementary funds with low fees.

mixed.label: Mixed
mixed.explanation: You combine several strategies. Thesion gives you a balanced mix of value, growth and dividends in its suggestions.

low.label: Low risk
low.explanation: We filter out speculative companies and small caps. Focus on large, established companies with low volatility. Investment plans are spread over time (DCA) to reduce timing risk.

medium.label: Medium risk
medium.explanation: A balance between stable large caps and more exciting growth cases. Investment plans are spread over 2-3 months.

high.label: High risk
high.explanation: You can tolerate large price swings. We include small caps and growth companies with higher potential. Investments are preferably made up front (lump sum) for the best historical return.

beginner.label: Beginner
beginner.explanation: Mats (the AI assistant) explains everything in simple terms and avoids jargon. Tooltips and explanations are shown extra clearly.

intermediate.label: Some experience
intermediate.explanation: Mats uses common financial terms but explains more advanced concepts. You get a good mix of guidance and depth.

advanced.label: Experienced
advanced.explanation: Mats provides in-depth analysis with key metrics, trends and comparisons without holding back.

importGuide.title: Import from Avanza
importGuide.subtitle: Step-by-step guide

step1.title: Log in to Avanza
step1.description: Go to avanza.se and log in with BankID.

step2.title: Go to Profile
step2.description: Click "Profil" in the left-hand menu (or at the bottom on mobile).

step4.title: Choose monthly statement
step4.description: Click the "Månadsbesked" tab. Choose account and period — then click the PDF link to open the report.
step4.tip: The report opens in a new tab. Save it locally: right-click → "Save as" or Cmd+S (Mac) / Ctrl+S (Windows).

step5.title: Import into Thesion
step5.description: Click "Import portfolio" here in Thesion and drag in the saved PDF file, or click to choose it.

step6.title: Review and confirm
step6.description: Thesion reads all holdings with number of shares and GAV (average acquisition cost). Review the list, adjust any ticker matches and click "Import".
step6.tip: Stocks already in your portfolio are marked as "Already exists" and are skipped.

importGuide.troubleBody: Make sure you download the report as a PDF (rather than opening it in the browser). The file is usually named something like "Månadsrapport_2026-03.pdf".

section1.title: 1. Who we are
section1.body: Thesion is a portfolio management service for stock market enthusiasts. The service is run as a hobby project and is provided as is.

section2.title: 2. What data we collect
section2.item1Text: Email address and an optional display name when you register.
section2.item2Text: Stocks, groups and settings you create in the service.
section2.item3Text: IP address and timestamps at login (handled by Supabase Auth).
section2.footer: We do not collect data via third-party cookies, tracking pixels or analytics tools.

section3.title: 3. How we store your data
section3.body: All data is stored in Supabase (PostgreSQL) on servers within the EU. Each user can only view and change their own data thanks to Row Level Security (RLS) at the database level. Communication always takes place over HTTPS.

section4.title: 4. How we use your data
section4.body: Your data is used solely to provide the service's features — showing your portfolio, fetching prices and generating key metrics. We never sell your data to third parties.

section5.title: 5. The AI assistant and your portfolio data
section5.body: Thesion has a built-in AI assistant (powered by Anthropic Claude). When you use the chat, your portfolio data — including stock holdings, number of shares, average cost and P&L — may be sent to Anthropic to provide personalised answers.
section5.item1Text: You can turn off sharing of portfolio data with the AI under Profile → Privacy & AI.
section5.item2Text: Anthropic does not use your data to train its models (Anthropic's terms of use).
section5.item3Text: Your portfolio data is not stored by Anthropic after the conversation.
section5.item4Text: Indices, commodities and public stock prices are always shared (not personal data).

section6.title: 6. Who has access to your data
section6.item1Text: Only you can see your portfolio, your holdings and your settings (protected by Row Level Security).
section6.item2Text: The project owner has technical access to the Supabase database for troubleshooting and support. This access is logged.
section6.item3Text: Supabase (data storage, EU), Anthropic (AI chat, when sharing is enabled), Vercel (hosting). None of these are given access without your consent.

section7.title: 7. Cookies
section7.body: We only use essential cookies for authentication (Supabase Auth). No advertising or analytics cookies are used.

section8.title: 8. Your rights (GDPR)
section8.item1: Request a copy of all data we hold about you.
section8.item3: Delete your account and all associated data.
section8.item4: Object to the processing of your data.

section9.title: 9. Contact
section9.body: Do you have questions about your data, or want to exercise your rights? Contact us at

allocationDocs.title: Portfolio allocation
allocationDocs.introPre: Thesion analyses your portfolio using the
allocationDocs.introPost: — an established strategy that splits the portfolio into three parts with different purposes. The analysis is shown as an allocation card on the Portfolio page, and Mats can comment on your allocation in the chat.
allocationDocs.coreSatelliteIntro: The model is built on having a stable core as the foundation, complemented with more offensive positions:
allocationDocs.coreDesc: Stable blue chips, defensive companies, low beta (<0.8), high quality. These provide safety and stability to the portfolio. Examples: large banks, telecom companies, healthcare giants, investment companies.
allocationDocs.satelliteDesc: Growth companies, thematic positions, medium risk. This is where you take positions in trends and sectors you believe in. Examples: SaaS companies, e-commerce, fintech, mid-caps with growth.
allocationDocs.speculationDesc: High risk, high upside, turnarounds. Small positions in companies with asymmetric potential. Examples: micro-caps, pre-revenue companies, crypto-related.
allocationDocs.classificationIntro: Each holding is classified using a points-based system that accumulates signals. Positive points pull towards Core, negative towards Speculation, and everything in between ends up as Satellite.
allocationDocs.thresholdText: Total score ≥ 3 → Core. Total score ≤ −3 → Speculation. Everything in between → Satellite.
allocationDocs.missingDataText: The holding is placed as Satellite (not Speculation) and is classified based on sector and name. This avoids companies being wrongly flagged as speculative just because they are not in our scoring database.
allocationDocs.targetAllocationIntro: The allocation card compares your current distribution against a target allocation based on your risk profile:
allocationDocs.balancedPre: Deviations are shown in percentage points (pp). The portfolio counts as
allocationDocs.balancedPost: if Core deviates at most ±10pp and Speculation at most ±5pp from the target.
allocationDocs.strategiesIntro: When you have money to invest, there are two main strategies for putting it into the market. Thesion adapts its recommendation based on your risk profile.
allocationDocs.lumpSumDef: means investing the entire amount immediately.
allocationDocs.dcaDef: means spreading the purchases out over time — for example the same amount every week or month.
allocationDocs.researchIntroPost: (2012) analysed data from the US, the UK and Australia between 1926–2011. The results show that:
allocationDocs.researchLi1Pre: Lump Sum beat DCA in roughly
allocationDocs.researchLi3: The reason: the market tends to rise over time, so money sitting on the sidelines misses out on returns
allocationDocs.sourceNote: Source: Vanguard Research, "Dollar-cost averaging just means taking risk later" (July 2012). Authors: Georgianni, Shtekhman & Tasopoulos.
allocationDocs.adaptIntro: Based on your risk profile, Mats recommends different strategies:
allocationDocs.lowRiskDesc: Spreads the risk as much as possible. You avoid worrying about timing and market swings.
allocationDocs.mediumRiskDesc: A balance between spreading risk and getting into the market quickly.
allocationDocs.highRiskDesc: Historically the best return. Suits you if you can handle swings and believe in the market long term.
allocationDocs.tipText: Whatever the strategy — the most important thing is to invest regularly and stick to your plan. Waiting for the "right moment" usually gives worse results than just getting started.
